title: ICE Fatally Shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston; No Body Cameras Present
excerpt: An ICE officer shot and killed 52-year-old Mexican construction contractor Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a traffic stop in Houston's East End. The officers involved were not wearing body cameras, and witnesses in the vehicle disputed the agency's claim that Salgado Araujo used his van as a weapon.
content:
On July 7, 2026, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican national who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer while driving his construction crew to a job site in Houston, Texas. He was pronounced dead at Ben Taub Hospital.

ICE described the shooting as a "targeted enforcement operation" and alleged Salgado Araujo tried to use his van as a weapon against agents — an account immediately disputed by three co-workers in the vehicle and later contradicted by a CNN source who reported Salgado Araujo was not even the intended target of the operation.

The officers involved were not equipped with body cameras. DHS attributed the absence to funding interruptions caused by government shutdowns in 2025 and 2026, even as body cameras had already been deployed to more than half of ICE field offices.

  • Witnesses told attorneys that ICE vehicles rammed the work van and agents were not at risk of being struck before the agent fired from the passenger side.
  • Salgado Araujo's passengers told lawyers they felt pressure from ICE agents to sign self-deportation papers while in custody.
  • The Harris County District Attorney announced an investigation, despite difficulty accessing federal evidence.
  • Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum announced she would request criminal charges over this and 16 other Mexican nationals killed in ICE operations.
  • Grand jury proceedings were subsequently reported underway by ABC13.
source: Texas Tribune / CNN / Houston Public Media
